Each item gets Tier 1 regressions that fail on 465354a and pass after the fix; pin EVERY v-adversarial probe from the previous round (S1-S24 where applicable, F1-E5, F4 reuse) as a regression with its exact expected component/status.

 Do not change other semantics. Run Tier 1 and Tier 2 locally; commit as Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>, message ending exactly:
${TRAILER}

 Never comment on PRs. Report new head, diff summary, test counts.`, { label: 'fix2', phase: 'Fix', schema: ITEMS })

TASK (label v2-adversarial; READ-ONLY): try to break G1-G6 with NEW variants beyond the previous probe set: YAML anchors/aliases/merge keys for name and run, multi-document files, flow style, block scalars with chomping indicators, tags, BOM, CRLF, tabs, duplicate keys (which value wins in GitHub's parser vs PyYAML), very long lines; confusables not covered by the chosen skeleton; scripts invoked via env indirection (\$SCRIPT), via 'python -m <module>' resolving to a tree module that calls Track C tools, via make/npm scripts, via a reusable workflow (uses: ./.github/workflows/x.yml), via 'bash -c' strings; side-file verifier bypasses; determinism breakers. TOP: AC-32.spoof is bypassed end to end at 523e702. Full CLI on S24V2 (3b09df4e…) gives FPIA_PASS, exit 0, INTEGRATION_INTERFERENCE_NONE, result_sha256 7a5a9f20…, VERIFIED.
- Two independent gaps are combined: an invisible trailing U+2800 in the name (outside UTS #39 and Default_Ignorable), and a rooted `cd ${{ github.workspace }}/…`, which `command()` never follows because its argument contains '$'.
- Either gap alone also passes: the static phase gives NONE for U01 and I01 on committed trees.

D1 bugs, where FPIA contradicts its own stated claim:
- Rooted cd / working-directory / `defaults.run.working-directory` with the workspace prefix (I01–I03, I29, I65).
- `bash -ec`, `sh -xc`, `bash -o pipefail <script>` and GitHub's own `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` (I08, I09, I15, I16).
- `cd -P` / `cd --` (I05, I06).
- Shebang-less local scripts silently skipped (I19).
- Backslash-newline joined with a space (I20).
- Fail-open on a shlex error per line (I51).
- `github.action_path` / `$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH` (I31, I32).
- NFKC applied before the 'UTS #39 skeleton', which loses five ICU confusables: U+02DB, U+037A, U+03F2, U+FE58, U+FFE8 (U27–U32).

D2 gaps, all fixable without a policy decision:
- GitHub literal-expression folding: `name`/`run-name` `${{ 'track-c-evl-validation' }}`, constant `format()`, `working-directory: ${{ '…' }}`, and a whole `run:` as one literal (Y27–Y30, Y41, Y42). The GitHub parser oracle shows the folded Track C values.
- Blank or invisible code points outside UTS #39 in the name or filename stem: U+2800, U+1D159, U+FFF9, U+16FE4, U+0131+U+0307, control characters.
- Wrappers and options: pushd, `env -C`, timeout, `nice -n`, `uv --directory`, CDPATH, `then cd`.
- Python: `python -m` with PYTHONPATH, literal `cwd=` / `os.chdir`, `pytest.main([...])`.
- Pytest: @argsfile, PYTEST_ADDOPTS, `-c` ini, `--ignore-glob`.
- Other launchers: make and npm scripts.
- Local node and docker actions, which are neither followed nor failed closed.
- Absolute runner workspace path; Windows backslash paths.

G5: the FPIA verdict, not only result_sha256, depends on the environment. FPIA_PASS becomes FPIA_FAIL (exit 1) for the same T and verifier when either:
- the interpreter is reached through a symlinked venv path (run3: 360 AC-28 findings for pytest's own plugins; `plugin_findings` compares a realpath with an unresolved path); or
- the work directory lies under a symlinked TMPDIR (run4: the v2 codex replay crashes in `relative_to`, AC-29 node-id mismatch, AC-35, spawn attribution lost).

This is a fail-closed direction (false FAIL), but macOS-style TMPDIRs (/var → /private/var) and symlinked venvs are ordinary setups. Fix: resolve the work dir and `sys.prefix` paths once up front.

Also: `result.integration_interference.spawns[].argv` contains `pytest-of-<OS user>`, so local (root) and CI (runner) result_sha256 can never match for trees with recorded spawns, such as acaf1b5.

G4: `--verify-output` VERIFIED does not cover the `run` section, even with the external anchor. That section holds the F2 transport disclosure, path_tokens, argv and fetch log; only `run.verbatim_raw` is declared.

It also accepts:
- duplicate top-level keys (a first-wins reader can be shown FPIA_FAIL or FPIA_PASS different from what is verified);
- side-file names with '../' (reads outside `<out>.verbatim/` and prints their sha256/size).

Read and write use the locale encoding: under an ASCII locale the verifier says NOT_RUN on a genuine file, and the writer crashes with exit 1, leaving an empty --out.

An --out under a missing directory is not preflighted: it crashes with exit 1 after the full audit and leaves the work directory behind.

The CI step runs `--verify-output` without `--expect-result-sha256`, so it checks self-consistency only.

G3: ref names containing U+2028, U+2029 or U+0085 hide their refusal lines, because `rejected_lines` uses `str.splitlines()`. `Sandbox.fetch` then returns rc 0 with `rejected []`. In the audit this is masked by the shallow pre-check, so the impact is low. Fix: split on '\n' only.
G6: verdicts are correct in all five cases. One wording gap: a tree carrying a Track C-namespace file that is not in R is labelled 'Track C not integrated in this tree' with count 0.

Holds:
- YAML decoding: anchors, aliases, merge keys, multi-doc fail-closed, flow, block chomping and indentation indicators, tags, BOM, CRLF, tabs, long lines, 1 MB file, deep nesting fail-closed.
- Duplicate keys: PyYAML keeps the last value, FPIA considers every value, and GitHub rejects the file, so FOUND is conservative.
- All 4174 Default_Ignorable insertions and 362 ICU-confusable substitutions are matched.
- Env indirection with a literal path; local reusable workflow and `python -m` tree module with literal paths; heredoc to bash; subshells; two-line cd; aliases for run and working-directory.
- Hash-seed independence of the static analysis.
- Consistent re-hash detected against the CI anchor; non-empty --out refused.
